'''Daniel Ioan Tătaru''' (born 6 May 1967) is a [[Romania]]n [[mathematician]] at [[University of California, Berkeley]]. 

He was born in [[Piatra Neamț]]. As a student at the [[Petru Rareș National College (Piatra Neamț)|Petru Rareș High School]], he won the National Mathematical Olympiad three times and the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] twice. He then studied mathematics at the [[Alexandru Ioan Cuza University|University of Iași]]. His 1990 diploma thesis, supervised by [[Viorel P. Barbu]], was on [[Hamilton–Jacobi equation]]s in [[Banach space]]s and nonlinear semigroups; it won the Gheorghe Țițeica Prize from the Romanian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="adevarul"/> Tătaru earned his doctorate from the [[University of Virginia]] in 1992, under supervision of [[Irena Lasiecka]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=53273 }}</ref> The next year he joined the faculty at [[Northwestern University]] and in 2001 he moved to Berkeley.<ref name="adevarul"/>

He won the 2002 [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]] for his research<ref name="Tataru 2001 pp. 37–77">{{cite journal | last=Tataru | first=Daniel | title=On global existence and scattering for the wave maps equation | journal=[[American Journal of Mathematics]] | volume=123 | issue=1 | date=2001 | issn=1080-6377 | doi=10.1353/ajm.2001.0005 | pages=37–77}}</ref> on [[partial differential equation]]s. In 2003, he was awarded the [[National Order of Merit (Romania)|Romanian Order of Merit]], Commander rank.<ref>{{citation| url=https://legislatie.just.ro/Public/DetaliiDocument/44401| title=Decret nr. 370 din 11 iunie 2003| language=ro|work=[[Monitorul Oficial]]| issue=420|date=June 16, 2003|access-date=May 28, 2025}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-08-25.</ref> In 2013 he was selected as a [[Simons Investigator]]<ref>[https://www.simonsfoundation.org/program-areas/mathematics-and-physical-science/simons-investigators/simons-investigators-2013/ Simons Investigator], www.simonsfoundation.org</ref> in mathematics. In 2023, he was elected honorary member of the [[Romanian Academy]].<ref name="adevarul">{{cite news|url=https://adevarul.ro/stiri-locale/piatra-neamt/profesor-roman-de-la-berkeley-noul-membru-de-2352938.html|title=Profesor român de la Berkeley, noul membru de onoare al Academiei Române. Daniel Ioan Tătaru este numit "Matematicianul secolului 21"|language=ro|newspaper = [[Adevărul]]|date=April 8, 2024|access-date=May 29, 2025}}</ref>
